messages:
sanjay: FYI getting an escalation from BrightCart on their Dedicated pool (acme-ded-2). They report recurring 429s and token-level latency spikes since ~03:10 UTC. Ticket INC-4921 opened. :rotating_light:

support-bot: Customer message: "we see intermittent 429s and responses taking 2-6s for short completions. App degraded since 03:10, started after autoscale events. Please advise."

ops-bot: [ALERT] autoscaler-flapping detected on acme-ded-2: scale events in last 12m = [+1, -1, +1, -2, +1] threshold breaches: cpu_util 78% -> 40% -> 82% -> 38%

elaine: Can you paste the recent autoscaler logs and any kube events? Also need which model/version they're pinned to and min/max replicas.

sanjay: Pinned to rwd-model-v2-quant, min_replicas=1, max_replicas=6. Autoscaler history attached (snippet):
```
2026-03-16T03:10:12Z scale_up from 1 to 2 reason=cpu>scale_up_threshold(75) util=78 cooldown_up=60s
2026-03-16T03:12:03Z scale_down from 2 to 1 reason=cpu<scale_down_threshold(45) util=40 cooldown_down=30s
2026-03-16T03:13:22Z scale_up from 1 to 2 reason=cpu>75 util=82 cooldown_up=60s
2026-03-16T03:15:05Z scale_down from 2 to 0 reason=cpu<45 util=38 cooldown_down=30s
```
Note the cooldowns are very short and min_replicas=1 so dropping to zero briefly.

aj: Dropping to 0 replicas is rough for warm start — KV caches get lost, causing QPS ripples and apparent 429s while instances spin up. We should never scale below 1 active backend for this pool. Also I suspect noisy neighbor: one tenant in that pool is running batch evals. Memory pressure + eviction cycles can oscillate util numbers.

elaine: Repro steps from customer: heavy chat bursts at 03:09-03:11 (prefix reuse small), then steady low QPS. They said spikes correlate with backend scale events.

cal: Proposed immediate mitigation (canary today): set min_replicas=2 for acme-ded-2, increase cooldown_up to 180s, cooldown_down to 300s, and enable smoothing window=120s (moving average on util). That should add hysteresis and avoid flip-flopping. Thoughts?

sanjay: +1 to not dropping to 0. Also recommend increasing scale_up_threshold to 85% to avoid aggressive upscales driven by transient bursts.

aj: For noisy neighbor limit: we can enable per-tenant GPUMemReservation or set sharing_policy=strict on the busiest nodes. For short term, move heavy tenant off acme-ded-2 to acme-ded-batch if possible.

elaine: Ops question — will higher cooldowns impact legitimate autoscale responsiveness for real sustained load? We need to balance. Suggest canary change for this pool and monitor 30m.

cal: I'll open a deployment PR to change autoscaler config for acme-ded-2 and patch rollout to only that pool. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/auto-config/pull/487 (canary -> prod if green).

ops-bot: [ACTION] Created incident INC-4921 and linked to PR-487. Pager duty alert created for oncall-rotation.

support-bot: Sent customer update: "We identified autoscaler oscillation causing warm cache loss and transient 429s. We're rolling a targeted tuning patch (min_replicas + cooldowns) and will update in 30m." :thumbsup:

aj: Followups to do: 1) add safeguard to never scale to 0 for pools serving low-latency models 2) add moving-average smoothing for the CPU/GPU util input 3) add a small startup-warmup weight so new replicas report warm=false until KV prefill complete.

elaine: I'll run a quick local simulation with current traffic pattern to estimate impact of cooldowns. If numbers look good, approve canary.

sanjay: Great. Thanks team. Marking this major customer escalation. Will update INC-4921 with config diffs and timeline. :eyes:
